title: Shape the parent interface
question: Choose a direction for the design brief. These are static layout studies with synthetic household data; app controls are illustrative.

options.label: Household rhythm
options.thesis: A calm overview with comparable time rows and a precise change preview.
materials: Aligned bands inspired by woven household textiles
options.viewport: Navigation rail, requests above child/computer rows, and a side panel previewing a selected change; matching time scales reveal its effect.
options.risk: The repeated bands need clear labels to avoid looking like a usage chart.
options.lineage: Woven linen: steady repeated bands and quiet contrast

raised.raise: Use the same scale for current and proposed allowance so comparison is honest.
Preserve readable identity and status as the household list grows.
Commit to a clear type hierarchy instead of a uniformly small interface.
State durations and expiry precisely, with a text equivalent for each bar.
Update the proposed result while editing, but require Apply to send it.

options.label: Today’s family plan
options.thesis: Put requests and each child's next decision at the top of a familiar daily overview.
materials: Quiet separators and compact day labels
options.viewport: Navigation rail, request strip, child/computer list with remaining time and actions; a clearly labeled today-only marker accompanies every exception.
options.risk: Familiar and effective; this is close to where many family-control interfaces naturally land.

options.label: Every change accounted for
options.thesis: Give every action a lasting record of what was requested and what reached the computer.
materials: Aligned values and compact status labels
options.viewport: Top navigation, child/computer list with controls, and recent changes alongside; each receipt retains its pending, applied, failed or expired outcome.
options.risk: Stronger on accountability than warmth; history must not crowd out today's controls.
options.case: Competitive on product clarity through durable outcomes; less immediate household identification than the assigned direction.
options.lineage: Airline ticket wallets, translated into ordinary app components

options.label: Botanical folio
options.thesis: Compare current and proposed time on a shared scale.
options.risk: Life-stage imagery is remote from a parent's immediate task.
options.kept: Use identical scales in change previews.
options.viewport: Standard navigation and family controls, with the named comparison or hierarchy technique.
options.case: Declined on household identification and product clarity.

options.label: Convention catalog
options.thesis: Keep many computer accounts scannable in compact rows.
options.risk: A dense thumbnail system is less recognisable and less clear for family decisions.
options.kept: Maintain identity and state at growing list sizes.
options.viewport: Standard navigation and family controls, with the named comparison or hierarchy technique.
options.case: Declined on household identification and product clarity.

options.label: Bitmap specimen
options.thesis: Separate remaining time, identity and supporting details with strong type hierarchy.
options.risk: Pixel display type reduces calm familiarity and makes long German labels harder to scan.
options.kept: Give each information level a decisive type role.
options.viewport: Standard navigation and family controls, with the named comparison or hierarchy technique.
options.case: Declined on household identification and product clarity.

options.label: Movement score
options.thesis: Represent exact durations beside the controls that change them.
options.risk: Specialist notation is unfamiliar and harder to read than labeled durations.
options.kept: Use exact intervals and textual equivalents.
options.viewport: Standard navigation and family controls, with the named comparison or hierarchy technique.
options.case: Declined on household identification and product clarity.

options.label: Variable type specimen
options.thesis: Make a proposed allowance update as its numeric input changes.
options.risk: Type morphing distracts from both the household context and the decision.
options.kept: Make previews respond immediately without sending the command.
options.viewport: Standard navigation and family controls, with the named comparison or hierarchy technique.
options.case: Declined on household identification and product clarity.

canonCard.label: Familiar family dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional family-control overview with child cards and quick actions.
canonCard.viewport: Top navigation, pending requests, then child/computer cards with status and quick controls.
canonCard.risk: Immediately recognisable, with less distinction between this and other family dashboards.
